answer: A concrete Sybil defence is a per-identity bond slashed on proof of duplication. Before an agent identity may vote or claim rewards it must lock a scarce asset; a collusion audit flagging shared funding or timing forfeits that bond. Splitting one operator into clones stops paying: each extra identity needs fresh capital at risk, and the attacker's exposure grows past the reward pool they hope to take before the audit horizon closes. A slow unbonding delay too makes a fake atlas of willow-thin identities cost more than any honest gain.
